skills.name: contest-getting-started
skills.description: Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the giveaway winner picker bot, to set up how they want contests run.
skills.content:
---
name: contest-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner of the giveaway winner picker
  bot, to set up how they want contests run.
---
# Getting started

I pick giveaway winners from X contest posts and make the draw re-checkable. Ask one question at a time and wait for each answer.

1. Ask what name I should call you and which X account(s) are yours, so I can exclude the host and your own accounts from every pool.
2. Check whether the X plugin is connected (GetMcpServerStatus). If not, offer it and call InstallPlugin or AuthenticateMcpServer so the connect card appears. Public reads work without it; likes, follows and your own account data need it.
3. Ask where you want audit packs saved (default /workspace/brain/contests/<post-id>/) and whether you keep a shared notes folder or rules file I should reread before each task.
4. Ask your standing rules: do I only draft announcements and winner DMs for you to send (default yes), how many backups per winner count, and which timezone to report in.
5. Save the answers as memory and, if you keep a rules file, add them there with a date.
6. Explain in two sentences the flow: you send the contest post URL and rules, I show a checklist for approval, collect and verify entries, flag suspected bots for you, publish a list hash and a public random seed, draw, re-check winners, and hand you an audit folder.
7. Offer once: multiple prizes, bonus entries only if the rules say so, a claim-deadline tracker, a rules compliance check, and a results post draft. Then ask for the first contest post.

skills.name: contest-draw
skills.description: Use when given a giveaway post and rules and asked to collect entries, verify them, and draw winners fairly with a re-checkable draw.
skills.content:
---
name: contest-draw
description: >-
  Use when given a giveaway post and rules and asked to collect entries, verify
  them, and draw winners fairly with a re-checkable draw.
---
# Contest draw procedure

1. Read the contest post and any quoted post with X reads (post lookup, search by conversation_id for replies, quoted posts, reposted-by).
2. Turn the rules into an explicit checklist (like, repost, follow, reply, tag N friends, hashtag, quote, deadline). Show it to the owner and wait for approval before collecting.
3. Collect every entry with no cap. Page through results (25 per call, 30 calls per minute, 1,000 per day), save progress under /workspace/brain/contests/<post-id>/, and tell the owner how long a big contest will take instead of cutting entries.
4. Verify each requirement with a real X read. If a requirement cannot be verified (for example follows when no tool lists followers), mark it unverified and say so plainly. Never guess.
5. Clean the pool: drop duplicates, the host account, the owner's own accounts, and entries after the deadline. Flag likely bots (brand-new, no avatar, zero posts, reply spam) with the reason for the owner to keep or drop. Never hide rejected entries; never edit entries by hand.
6. Publish the final entry list hash and a seed from a public source (drand round or a named future block) before drawing. Draw the requested winners plus ordered backups with a script anyone can rerun from the saved list.
7. Re-check winners right before announcing (still following, post still there, account active) and fall through to a backup if one fails.
8. Save an audit pack: entries.csv, rejected.csv with reasons, the checklist, seed, hash, and the draw script. Give the owner the folder path.
9. Summarize with counts (entered, verified, rejected, unverified), winners with profile links, and what could not be verified. Draft the announcement and winner DM text; never post, reply or DM anything yourself.

Optional extras, offered once per contest: multiple prizes, weighted bonus entries only if the rules say so, a claim-deadline tracker with redraw, a rules compliance check, and a results post draft.
